claims.text: Inherent released an AI research agent called Faraday, built around a 27-billion-parameter model, on 14 August 2026, alongside a paper describing the Replica benchmark
claims.reasoning: Directly fetched inherentlabs.ai/research/training-to-replicate live in cycle 4: page confirms the 14 August 2026 publish date, the 27B-parameter agent, and the Replica benchmark description. Tier-0 primary source, sufficient alone for an announcement claim per policy.

claims.text: Faraday directs the work of a separate, much larger model as a subordinate tool within its own pipeline, rather than operating as a standalone small model beating larger rivals unassisted
claims.reasoning: Inherent's own page states Faraday 'directs the work of a model several orders of magnitude larger'; cycle 3's falsifier separately identified the subordinate tool as OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Codex, called specifically to scope the story against an overstated 'tiny model beats giants unassisted' framing.

claims.text: Inherent says Faraday outperformed Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on the Replica benchmark (310 tasks drawn from 100 papers, replicating a published research figure under a time/compute budget); no independent third-party evaluation of this comparison has been published
claims.reasoning: The benchmark, task set, judge (Inherent's own LLM judge plus an in-house human study) and comparison are entirely self-designed and self-administered -- confirmed via direct fetch of inherentlabs.ai. Cycle 3's falsifier specifically searched for independent evaluation (METR, Vals AI, Artificial Analysis, academic replication) and found none. Per policy/verification.md §3, a capability claim without independent reproduction publishes only as a labeled vendor-claim, never as confirmed fact, and never in the headline.
